subject: Specifying a mirt model using contents of SingleGroupClass object

messages.author: 6e50d514a7c719fe
messages.subject: Specifying a mirt model using contents of SingleGroupClass object
parts:
Hi Phil et al, 

Let's say we have:

###
data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod1 <- mirt(data, 1)
###

I want to now fit the same model specified in the above call to mirt() but using new data. If one is familiar with the update() function, what I want is to basically do something akin to:

###
data2 <- data[-1,] #remove first row
mod2 <- update(mod1,data=data2) #doesn't actually work
###

where mod2 will have the same IRT model estimated in the original call to mirt (which yielded mod1) but now applied to data2. Essentially, I want to reconstruct the oroiginal call to mirt() using the elements of the SingleGroupClass object mod1.

My sense is that everything one would need to do it is contained in the mod1 object. You can get, for example, itemtype info:

###
mod1@Model$itemtype
###

but I can't see a way of easily repackaging all the relevant information. Is there an efficient way of doing this (e.g., I had hoped there might be a function which converted elements of mod1 into a model specification object along the lines of what is returned by mirt.model)? Thanks in advance for any help and, while I searched the archives, apologies if I missed a previous post on this.

Ben

PS-Another thought I had was to use the information in mod1@Call, but I think that elements of that would need to be parsed in the same environment as the original call and I don't think that would work in the generic case I have in mind.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Specifying a mirt model using contents of SingleGroupClass object
parts:
Hi Ben,

Not quite sure if this is what you're looking for, but using home-grown functions on the fly are pretty good for this type of thing. Here's an example:

########
library(mirt)
data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod1 <- mirt(data)

my_mirt <- function(index, data, ...){
    dd <- data[-index, , drop=FALSE]
    mod <- mirt(dd, ...)
    mod
}

mods <- sapply(seq(1,1000, by=100), my_mirt,
               data=data, itemtype = '3PL')
lapply(mods, coef, simplify=TRUE)
#####

Functions like update() would be nice but AFAIK they are only useful when the input is a simple formula type. HTH for now.


Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Specifying a mirt model using contents of SingleGroupClass object
parts:
Hmm, I don't believe something like this exists in a user-friendly form, but I'm interested in adding a function that could do this as it would be less clunky in other areas of the package (e..g, PLCI.mirt(), boot.mirt(), etc). Something along the lines of 

model_specs <- extract_model.specs(prev.mirt.model)
new.model <- mirt(newdata, model_specs=model_specs)

Would that work for you?

Phil


On Tue, Aug 13, 2024 at 8:36 PM Ben Domingue <ben.do...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil, 

Thanks for the response! My definition of data2 may have been misleading; the removal of the first row was just to motivate data2 as a 'novel' dataset. The real goal is to be able to completely specify the non-data parts of the second call to mirt() using the elements stored in the first call. To better motivate what I want, consider:

###

library(mirt)
data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod1 <- mirt(data)

mod2 <- mirt(data[-1,],itemtype=mod1@Model$itemtype)
###

The goal would be to specify a call as in the assignment to mod2 that replicates the model specified in mod1. It's simple here given that we fit a very simple model, but I'm trying to figure out a way of handling the generic case where the specification in mod1 may be much more complex. It might be that such functionality is not yet implemented; even knowing that is the case would be useful. 

Thanks! Ben
